pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/__tests__/components/CrashAnalyzerImport.no-diagnosis.test.tsx:47 The import test swaps the store's real importCrashLog for a test-written version that replaces `reports` wholesale. The shipped action (src/stores/crashAnalyzerStore.ts:97) sets isLoading/error and merges re-imports by id, so the green 'no diagnosis' UI result describes a program no user runs.

techniques.evidence: src/__tests__/components/CrashAnalyzerImport.no-diagnosis.test.tsx:47 The helper restates the store action rather than sharing it. It drops the real merge-by-id, isLoading and error handling, and its neutral name does not say what it leaves out.

src/__tests__/components/CrashHealthMap.test.tsx:20 The test name claims the empty hint, but the only assertion (line 22) is zero health-nodes, which a component returning null would also satisfy. The 'No crashes to map yet' branch is never asserted.

src/__tests__/api/crash-analyzer-history-route.test.ts:20 The pid-keyed throwaway DB and its -wal/-shm files are deleted before the import graph opens, so this run inherits nothing from a previous one.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/__tests__/api/milestone-deadlines-label.test.ts:10 Several route tests here (milestone-deadlines-*, telemetry-*, project-progress-empty-payload) create a pid-keyed temp DB that they never delete and never clear at start. Because Windows reuses pids, a later run can reopen an earlier run's rows inside the global sweep's 30-minute age floor, unlike sibling tests that unlink first or rmSync in afterAll.

techniques.evidence: src/__tests__/api/milestone-deadlines-label.test.ts:10 The scratch DB names no reaper of its own and is not reset at startup, so the 'from the previous run: nothing' rule depends on an age-floored backstop that the harness itself says can miss pid reuse. A sibling, project-rules-scope.test.ts:27, does reap its own DB.
src/__tests__/api/telemetry-scan-same-ms.test.ts:28 The same-millisecond collision is forced by freezing the clock rather than hoping two real scans land in one ms.
src/__tests__/api/project-progress-empty-payload.test.ts:12 The test records in its own comment that it was observed failing against the defect it guards.

pairs.registryProposal: isolation-lanes could state whether a harness-level startup sweep with an age floor (needed so concurrent runs keep their live files) satisfies 'launchers reap stale leftovers at startup' when scratch names are keyed by a reusable id such as a pid. Here the sweep and the pid key together leave a 30-minute inheritance window.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/__tests__/components/layout-lab/LayoutLab.skipLink.test.tsx:38 The skip-link test waits 600 ms of wall clock for the AnimatePresence exit to finish before asserting that the old view's DOM is gone. On a loaded 16-worker run the exit can outlast the sleep, so a schedule event is being asserted with a stopwatch.

techniques.evidence: src/__tests__/components/layout-lab/LayoutLab.skipLink.test.tsx:38 It uses a real sleep instead of awaiting the exit-complete event, waitFor on the DOM removal, or fake timers.
src/__tests__/components/layout-lab/shellTypeFloor.scan.test.ts:14 The structural pin strips comments from its haystack, so prose about the rule cannot satisfy or trip the needle.
src/__tests__/components/layout-lab/shellTypeFloor.scan.test.ts:24 The counter is proved on a known-bad input, including a comment decoy, before it is trusted on the real files.
e2e/catalog-pipeline-walker.spec.ts:15 The e2e walk of the /layout UI runs against a hermetic SQLite file that is wiped each run, never the operator DB.

e2e/catalog-pipeline-walker.spec.ts:32 The walker declares the expected population, and walk-status is written only when every expected pipeline walked (e2e/helpers/walk-status.ts:46), so a --grep subset cannot pass as the full run.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/__tests__/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-cancel.test.ts:51 The cancel test sleeps 10 ms of wall clock to 'let the worker pool dispatch its first in-flight passes' before aborting. If dispatch has not happened yet the abort lands pre-dispatch and the assertions still pass, so the in-flight cancel path the test exists for may go unexercised without any signal.

techniques.evidence: src/__tests__/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-cancel.test.ts:51 A timed sleep stands in for 'a pass is in flight'. By contrast, deep-eval-job.test.ts:217 does it right by asserting the recorded in-flight count (maxInFlight <= 4).

src/__tests__/lib/prompts/golden.ts:83 The deep-eval pass prompt golden (off-rail-join.test.ts:176, built from module-eval-prompts) re-records whenever an env var is set or the file is missing, and passes when it does. That is a second record path with no integrity test, so a deleted golden goes green.
src/__tests__/lib/evaluator/review-runner.test.ts:28 The review-runner ledger tests run in a mkdtemp scratch dir that names its reaper after every test.
